items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: He’s started an octet with two saxophones, just him and myself... I’m very honored to be asked by such a great writer to write, and by such a great saxophone player to be the other saxophone in his band.

ctx.x: Interesting. You’ve done some writing too, is that correct?

Yeah. On the new record I chose not to do any composing. I just wanted to arrange. I did arrangements of a lot of Duke things and some different, kind of obscure tunes. But yeah I like to write, I like to compose. Frank Wess asked me to do some writing for him. He’s started an octet with two saxophones, just him and myself, and two trumpets and a trombone. It’s a really nice little band, and I’m very honored to be asked by such a great writer to write, and by such a great saxophone player to be the other…
Cool. What about — you’ve also done some writing for publications?

items.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You have Ted Nash, can you mention all the players. Yeah, Ted Nash, Scott Robinson, Frank Greene, myself...

ctx.x: I have the players right here. You have Ted Nash, can you mention all the players.

Yeah, Ted Nash, Scott Robinson, Frank Greene, myself, Winard Harper on drums, and Peter Washington is doing part of the week and then I have Noreko, she’s a female Japanese bass player who plays with Diva. Then Michael Weiss is doing half of the week; he’s usually with me. I’ve done a lot of things with Michael. The last three days Tomoko Ohno is going to play with me, she’s worked with me before. I’ve taken her on gigs with me up in Connecticut and around. She’s a very good player; they’re both very good.
